transcript.text: Every so often when I use the hob the electrics in the house go off. Not every time, maybe once a week. It's an induction hob, Hisense I think.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. Because your induction hob is tripping the main electrics (likely an RCD), this indicates an earth leakage fault. This is a safety-critical issue where electricity is escaping to the metal casing of the hob. The most likely causes are:
1. A fault in the induction power module or coil for one of the zones.
2. Moisture ingress under the glass (if there was a recent spill).
3. A loose or damaged mains connection at the back of the hob. To help narrow this down safely, please tell me: Does the trip happen immediately when you switch any zone on, or only after a few minutes? Does it happen on all zones equally, or is there one specific zone that always causes it? Important safety note: Until an engineer has checked this, do not keep resetting the breaker to use the hob. If you smell burning plastic or see scorch marks, stop using it immediately and isolate the power at the fused spur/consumer unit.

It's not straight away, it seems to be when I've got two rings on high, and sometimes when something boils over. I haven't noticed if it's one particular ring. Once there was a faint electrical smell afterwards too.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. The combination of tripping when multiple zones are on high power and the faint electrical smell points to an earth leakage fault inside the hob. In an induction hob, this is typically caused by a failing induction coil or its associated power module leaking electricity to the metal casing. The boil-overs may have contributed by allowing moisture to seep in and exacerbate the issue, but the underlying cause is likely internal electrical degradation. Because this involves mains voltage and earth leakage, it is not safe for you to investigate further or attempt a repair yourself. You must leave the hob isolated (switched off at the fused spur or consumer unit) until a qualified engineer has inspected it. They will need to perform insulation resistance tests on the internal components that are unsafe for owners to access. Please do not use the hob again until this has been checked.

candidates: Earth leakage fault (induction coil or power module) (high)
